objectives.text: In order to guard against money laundering and the financing of terrorism through financial institutions, each financial institution shall establish anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism programs

citations.quote: In order to guard against money laundering and the financing of terrorism through financial institutions, each financial institution shall establish anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism programs, including, at a minimum-

objectives.text: AML/CFT programs should be reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the requirements of the subchapter and regulations promulgated under it

citations.quote: reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the requirements of this subchapter and regulations promulgated under this subchapter; and

objectives.text: AML/CFT programs should be risk-based, directing more attention and resources toward higher-risk customers and activities rather than lower-risk customers and activities

citations.quote: risk-based, including ensuring that more attention and resources of financial institutions should be directed toward higher-risk customers and activities, consistent with the risk profile of a financial institution, rather than toward lower-risk customers and activities.

objectives.text: Effective AML/CFT programs are understood to safeguard national security and generate public benefits by preventing the flow of illicit funds and assisting law enforcement and national security agencies

citations.quote: Effective anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism programs safeguard national security and generate significant public benefits by preventing the flow of illicit funds in the financial system and by assisting law enforcement and national security agencies with the identification and prosecution of persons attempting to launder money and undertake other illicit activity through the financial system.

obligations.action: establish anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism programs including, at a minimum, (A) development of internal policies, procedures, and controls; (B) designation of a compliance officer; (C) an ongoing employee training program; and (D) an independent audit function to test programs
obligations.trigger: In order to guard against money laundering and the financing of terrorism through financial institutions

obligations.action: prescribe minimum standards for programs established under paragraph (1), and exempt from those standards any financial institution not subject to part 103 of title 31 CFR (or successor rule) for so long as it remains not subject to such rules
obligations.trigger: after consultation with the appropriate Federal functional regulator
exceptions: financial institution not subject to the provisions of the rules contained in part 103 of title 31, of the Code of Federal Regulations, or any successor rule thereto, for so long as such financial institution is not subject to the provisions of such rules

citations.quote: The Secretary of the Treasury, after consultation with the appropriate Federal functional regulator (as defined in section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act), may prescribe minimum standards for programs established under paragraph (1), and may exempt from the application of those standards any financial institution that is not subject to the provisions of the rules contained in part 103 of title 31, of the Code of Federal Regulations, or any successor rule thereto, for so long as such financial institution is not subject to the provisions of such rules.

obligations.actor: Secretary of the Treasury and the appropriate Federal functional regulator
obligations.action: take into account listed factors (private compliance benefit, underbanked/remittance policy goals, national-security value of effective programs, and that programs should be reasonably designed and risk-based) in prescribing minimum standards and in supervising and examining compliance
obligations.trigger: In prescribing the minimum standards under subparagraph (A), and in supervising and examining compliance with those standards

citations.quote: In prescribing the minimum standards under subparagraph (A), and in supervising and examining compliance with those standards, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the appropriate Federal functional regulator (as defined in section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( 12 U.S.C. 6809 )) shall take into account the following:

obligations.action: prescribe regulations governing maintenance of concentration accounts by financial institutions, in order to ensure that such accounts are not used to prevent association of a customer's identity with the movement of the customer's funds

citations.quote: The Secretary may prescribe regulations under this subsection that govern maintenance of concentration accounts by financial institutions, in order to ensure that such accounts are not used to prevent association of the identity of an individual customer with the movement of funds of which the customer is the direct or beneficial owner, which regulations shall, at a minimum-

obligations.action: not allow clients to direct transactions that move their funds into, out of, or through the financial institution's concentration accounts
obligations.trigger: if the Secretary prescribes regulations under subsection (h)(3) governing concentration accounts

citations.quote: prohibit financial institutions from allowing clients to direct transactions that move their funds into, out of, or through the concentration accounts of the financial institution;

obligations.action: not inform customers of the existence of, or the means of identifying, the institution's concentration accounts
obligations.trigger: if the Secretary prescribes regulations under subsection (h)(3) governing concentration accounts

citations.quote: prohibit financial institutions and their employees from informing customers of the existence of, or the means of identifying, the concentration accounts of the institution; and

obligations.action: establish written procedures governing documentation of all transactions involving a concentration account, ensuring that when a transaction commingles funds of one or more customers, the identity of and specific amount belonging to each customer is documented
obligations.trigger: if the Secretary prescribes regulations under subsection (h)(3) governing concentration accounts

citations.quote: require each financial institution to establish written procedures governing the documentation of all transactions involving a concentration account, which procedures shall ensure that, any time a transaction involving a concentration account commingles funds belonging to 1 or more customers, the identity of, and specific amount belonging to, each customer is documented.

obligations.action: establish and make public priorities for anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism policy, in consultation with the Attorney General, Federal functional regulators, relevant State financial regulators, and relevant national security agencies
obligations.trigger: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this paragraph

citations.quote: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this paragraph, the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Attorney General, Federal functional regulators (as defined in section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( 15 U.S.C. 6809 )), relevant State financial regulators, and relevant national security agencies, shall establish and make public priorities for anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism policy.

obligations.action: update the AML/CFT priorities established under subparagraph (A)
obligations.trigger: Not less frequently than once every 4 years

citations.quote: Not less frequently than once every 4 years, the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Attorney General, Federal functional regulators (as defined in section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( 15 U.S.C. 6809 )), relevant State financial regulators, and relevant national security agencies, shall update the priorities established under subparagraph (A).

obligations.action: ensure that the priorities established under subparagraph (A) are consistent with the national strategy for countering the financing of terrorism and related forms of illicit finance

citations.quote: The Secretary of the Treasury shall ensure that the priorities established under subparagraph (A) are consistent with the national strategy for countering the financing of terrorism and related forms of illicit finance developed under section 261 of the Countering Russian Influence in Europe and Eurasia Act of 2017 ( Public Law 115–44 ; 131 Stat. 934 ).

obligations.actor: Secretary of the Treasury (acting through the Director of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network)
obligations.action: promulgate regulations to carry out the priorities paragraph, as appropriate, in consultation with Federal functional regulators and relevant State financial regulators
obligations.trigger: Not later than 180 days after the date on which the Secretary of the Treasury establishes the priorities under subparagraph (A)

citations.quote: Not later than 180 days after the date on which the Secretary of the Treasury establishes the priorities under subparagraph (A), the Secretary of the Treasury, acting through the Director of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and in consultation with the Federal functional regulators (as defined in section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( 15 U.S.C. 6809 )) and relevant State financial regulators, shall, as appropriate, promulgate regulations to carry out this paragraph.

obligations.actor: Secretary of the Treasury and appropriate Federal functional regulator (as supervisors/examiners)
obligations.action: include a financial institution's review of the established priorities and the incorporation of those priorities, as appropriate, into its risk-based AML/CFT programs as a measure on which the institution is supervised and examined for compliance with its obligations

citations.quote: The review by a financial institution of the priorities established under subparagraph (A) and the incorporation of those priorities, as appropriate, into the risk-based programs established by the financial institution to meet obligations under this subchapter, the USA PATRIOT Act ( Public Law 107–56 ; 115 Stat. 272 ), and other anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism laws and regulations shall be included as a measure on which a financial institution is supervised and examined for compliance with those obligations.

obligations.actor: persons in the United States (on behalf of the financial institution)
obligations.action: remain responsible for, and perform, the duty to establish, maintain and enforce the AML/CFT program, being accessible to and subject to oversight and supervision by the Secretary of the Treasury and the appropriate Federal functional regulator

citations.quote: The duty to establish, maintain and enforce an anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism program as required by this subsection shall remain the responsibility of, and be performed by, persons in the United States who are accessible to, and subject to oversight and supervision by, the Secretary of the Treasury and the appropriate Federal functional regulator (as defined in section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act ( 15 U.S.C. 6809 )).

notes: Extraction limited to subsection (h) 'Anti-Money Laundering Programs' (the program/'pillars' establishment obligations) and the closely bound concentration-account regulatory authority under (h)(3), plus the definitional cross-reference to GLBA Federal functional regulator, consistent with ratified scope excluding SAR/CTR/CDD coordination-layer duties (subsections (g), (i), (j), (k), (l)) and OFAC/sanctions/state-law boundary regimes found elsewhere in this section. Text preserved as written, including the internally inconsistent numbering note that subsec. (a)(5) was redesignated (a)(6) (see 'f' note) and the fact that subsection (h) applies to 'each financial institution' generically rather than being sector-specific to depository institutions, MSBs, or broker-dealers by its own terms; sector-specificity for pillars obligations as applied to MSBs/broker-dealers/banks arises from implementing regulations and SRO rules not contained in this statutory text. Modality for (h)(1) rendered as 'must' per 'shall establish'; concentration-account sub-obligations rendered 'conditional' because they only bind 'if' the Secretary exercises the discretionary rulemaking power in the lead-in of (h)(3), which itself uses 'may prescribe.'
